Jim —

Thanks for the context and the spec. Quick read: your growth profile matches several recent deals we’ve done that used a three-tranche onramp:

- Tranche A (weeks 0–6): small reserved pool (20–30% of 3–month expected steady state) + cloud backstop for peak bursts
- Tranche B (weeks 6–12): ramp to ~60% reserved; OEM order placed at week 4 to hit shipment window around week 10
- Tranche C (week 12+): full reserved commits as OEM freight completes and customs clears; cloud fallback scales down

Two sequencing items to confirm from your side: preferred OEM partners (we can coordinate quotes), and whether you want Redwood to hold an "interim reserved" pool (short-month reserved capacity we can scale down if needed) to limit early cloud costs.

Deliverables I’ll send after we align: a tranche-ladder timeline PDF, an OEM quote checklist (required SKU/RMA/cert info), and a candidate cloud-reserve plan that maps to triggers (latency breach, queue length, token/sec thresholds).

Propose a short sync Wed 5/20 to agree on OEM ask list and lead-time tolerances. Calendar link: https://cal.com/laura/30min?cid=acme-onramp

Team —

Attaching a quick tranche proposal (sheet + notes). High-level notes:

- SKU split: recommend mixing 80GB and 48GB nodes in early tranches to balance throughput and lead time risk. 80GB lines give better steady-state unit economics; 48GB are easier to procure quickly.
- OEM ask window: request preliminary quotes within 7 business days; firm PO by week 4. Most OEM lanes are quoting 10–14 week lead times today, but there are shorter "staging pool" options if you accept higher per-unit costs.
- Cloud backstop: propose a policy mapping - if 95th percentile latency > 150ms for 10 consecutive minutes, automatically route excess to cloud-reserve.
- Customs/port slack: build a 2-week buffer for cross-border freight; if Acme chooses expedited freight, adjust cost model accordingly.

Action items for Acme: confirm preferred OEM partners (NVIDIA OEM-A, HyperCompute LLC, or open to Redwood vendor introductions), and prioritize whether latency SLO or unit-cost is the stronger constraint — we’ll optimize the tranche mix accordingly.
